name: William Parker
bio: A groom, brother of Charles Parker, present at the pick-up in the St James's Restaurant bar and at the Rupert Street dinner where Wilde fed Charles from his own fork and spoon and passed him a preserved cherry mouth-to-mouth. He understood from the outset that the brothers 'were to be treated as women, and that you were to have money for it'; he went twice to Little College Street, shared Taylor's bed with his brother one night — his testimony describes an attempted sodomy by Taylor — then took country work as a groom and 'had nothing more to do with Taylor or with Mr. Wilde.' Taylor was convicted of gross indecency with him (count 9) on 21 May 1895.
bio_sources: William Parker's testimony, Hyde, Trials (1948), pp. 198-199 (p. 199 read as IIIF page image 2026-08-03)
Verdict at Taylor's trial, Hyde, Trials (1948), p. 292 (IIIF page image 2026-08-03)
Taylor's account of the brothers staying a week, Hyde, Trials (1948), p. 284 (djvu OCR)
bio_note: No birth/death dates or age found in sources read so far. Ellen Grant put Taylor's visitors at 'sixteen to thirty'; no source read states William's age. Taylor said he ultimately 'persuaded William Parker to go home to his father' (p. 284, djvu OCR). DATES: NOT FOUND; RECORDED AS UNRECOVERED FROM THE SOURCES CONSULTED (2026-08-03). Unlike his brother Charles, William gave no age on oath in the Hyde text: his examination-in-chief opens simply 'WILLIAM PARKER, examined by Mr. C. F. GILL - I am brother of Charles Parker. I have been employed as a groom' (located in the IA OCR text of Hyde; the neighbouring page carrying Charles's sworn age was verified at the page image, this passage was not). McKenna, Secret Life (2008), repo PDF p. 341, reports only Taylor's guess that the two brothers 'were sixteen or seventeen, or thereabouts' when he met them - a bystander's estimate of two people at once, not an age statement, and nothing is inferred from it. SWEEP FOR DATES, 2026-08-03 (what was searched): the Complete Letters (2000) OCR mirror plus the General Index; McKenna, The Secret Life of Oscar Wilde (2008), repo PDF; Murray, Bosie (2020), repo PDF; Frankel, The Unrepentant Years (2017), repo PDF; Hyde, The Trials of Oscar Wilde, in the Internet Archive copy (item in.ernet.dli.2015.499238, OCR text downloaded and searched, key pages then read as page images); and the open web. No birth or death date is recorded in any source consulted.
